| [NOTE-034](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-034.md) v3 | Curry et al. 2019, morality-as-cooperation in 60 societies | Coding 3,460 eHRAF paragraphs on the 60 Probability Sample Files societies found 962 morally valenced mentions of seven cooperative behaviours, 961 of them positive. | [NOTE-132](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-132.md) v2 | Moral disciplining: foundations of puritanical morality | Puritanical norms (condemning lust, gluttony, intoxicants, immodesty, idleness; praising temperance and piety) are argued to be cooperative morality after all: people believe cooperation needs self-control and that indulgence erodes it (and discipline trains it), so a single harm/fairness-sensitive moral system condemns victimless pleasures as indirect, probabilistic threats to cooperation. | [NOTE-185](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-185.md) | The moral psychology of obligation | Tomasello proposes that the human sense of obligation is "the internalized social/rational pressure from a joint or collective self-regulating agent 'we'… to do what 'we' expect me to" (§3). | [NOTE-400](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-400.md) | Haidt & Joseph 2004, intuitive ethics | An essay, not a study. Humans are innately prepared to feel quick approval or disapproval at four patterns, suffering, hierarchy, reciprocity and purity, each a module with an evolved proper domain and a culturally widened actual domain; ingroup is the best fifth candidate (fn. 15). | [NOTE-402](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-402.md) | The Evolution of Reciprocal Altruism | A verbal model: altruists who withhold help from non-reciprocators beat non-altruists when benefit exceeds cost, encounters are many, partners stable and exposure symmetric. | [NOTE-403](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-403.md) | Haidt 2001, the social intuitionist model | The social intuitionist model: moral judgments appear in consciousness as quick intuitions with an affective valence, and moral reasoning is usually a post-hoc search for supporting reasons, used to persuade others. Six links are drawn, four of them reasoning links, two of them private. The case rests on dual-process research, motivated reasoning, post-hoc confabulation and the weak tie between moral reasoning and moral action, mostly from outside morality. Harmless taboo violations are condemned regardless, and affect predicts the condemnation better than perceived harm. | Read |
| [NOTE-405](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-405.md) | Rai & Fiske 2011, relationship regulation | A theoretical review. Moral psychology is the regulation of social relationships: an act is right or wrong according to the relational model participants and observers apply, not according to its harm, fairness or purity in the abstract. Fiske's four models (communal sharing, authority ranking, equality matching, market pricing) each carry a moral motive: Unity, Hierarchy, Equality, Proportionality. Honour killing, obedient massacre, blood feud and collateral damage are each read as one motive at work. Purity and ingroup loyalty are both Unity. No new data are reported. | Read |

| [NOTE-407](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-407.md) | Baumard, André & Sperber 2013, mutualistic morality | Partner choice with outside options constrains how the gains of cooperation are split: nobody accepts less than they could get elsewhere, so with equal options the stable split is proportional to each partner's contribution of effort and talent. Being chosen then rewards a genuine sense of fairness over calculated fairness. Dictator, ultimatum, trust and public-goods results are read as allocations by perceived entitlement. Twenty-eight commentators accept partner choice and dispute that fairness is all of morality; the authors reply with a broad and a narrow position they have not settled between them. | Read |
| [NOTE-408](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-408.md) | Curry 2016, morality as cooperation: a problem-centred approach | The founding statement of morality-as-cooperation. | [NOTE-412](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-412.md) | Curry, Jones Chesters & Van Lissa 2019, the MAC-Q | A 42-item questionnaire for morality-as-cooperation's seven domains, written by the authors from the theory and reduced to three items per subscale. The two sets cannot be pooled into seven domains (CFI .73); the best model keeps fourteen correlated factors. The MFQ's five factors are not recovered.
